stem: A pharmacy receives a faxed Schedule II narcotic prescription that will be compounded for direct administration to the patient by continuous intravenous infusion. The prescription otherwise meets federal requirements. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The fax may serve as the original under the qualifying compounded-parenteral/infusion exception.
The fax can never be the original because compounding makes the drug Schedule I.
The exception applies only to oral compounded capsules.
The fax is valid only if the drug is nonnarcotic.
A technician may choose a different route to make the fax exception apply.

explanation.core_reasoning: Federal law permits the fax to serve as original for a qualifying Schedule II narcotic compounded for specified direct parenteral or infusion administration.

choice_analysis.A: The described route and narcotic fit the exception.
choice_analysis.C: The rule identifies qualifying parenteral/infusion routes.
choice_analysis.D: The exception is for a qualifying C-II narcotic.
choice_analysis.E: The prescribed route and clinical order control.

related_facts: The exception includes specified IV, IM, SC, and intraspinal uses under the regulation.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming every compounded C-II or every fax qualifies.

reasoning_steps: Classify the prescription as a Schedule II narcotic
